prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original fan-made production sprite sheet for a side-view tactical video game, faithful to Metal Gear Solid V The Phantom Pain (1984). EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows, exactly 16 independently DRAWN full-body poses of ONE same character. Pure flat magenta #FF00FF canvas with five thin continuous pure cyan #00FFFF vertical grid lines and five horizontal grid lines, including outer boundaries. Each equal square cell must contain exactly one complete character, wholly inside, generous empty margin at least 30 pixels, no extremity or equipment on guides. Fixed camera, strict orthographic RIGHT-facing profile, feet bottom aligned, identical physical scale every frame. Detailed crisp military pixel art, clear small-scale silhouette, no scenery, no ground shadow, no text, no labels, no logos, no watermark. The sixteen poses must be genuinely different drawings, never simple shifted duplicates. Four phases per row in left-to-right time order, preserve all costume and identity features in EVERY pose. Keep weapons and hands compact inside their cell. Subject: Dr Huey Emmerich in MGSV The Phantom Pain 1984, not Peace Walker wheelchair. Slender middle-aged man with round wire-frame glasses, messy medium dark-brown hair parted to sides, light stubble, worried posture. Light blue shirt with narrow darker vertical stripes, sleeves rolled to elbow, loose green necktie, dark gray trousers, brown shoes. Essential identity: external articulated gray metal EXOSKELETON supporting BOTH legs, mechanical hip belt with round motor housings, side thigh struts, knee hinges and shin rods to the sole plates. Not full body robot armour. Faithful to Konami official portrait and Shinkawa Huey + exoskeleton concepts. Row1 four idle balanced standing stages, subtle hands and nervous posture. Row2 four compact slow mechanically assisted right-facing stepping phases, hip/knee brace joints follow his own legs, heel contact, compression, passing and opposite contact. Row3 four checking a compact handheld wired controller stages; attached cable stays inside cell, no lettering. Row4 four small startled forward hunch and recover poses, RIGHT-facing head and body throughout. No wheelchair, no lab coat obscuring mechanical leg braces, no gun, no white decorative marks.

references.kind: secondary mirror of attributed Konami/Shinkawa concept and game model

notes: Complete authored poses, right-facing readable identity and distinctive mobility/costume maintained.
Code Talker uses seated wheelchair motion; Huey uses both external leg braces; Eli retains child proportions as applicable.
Pixel-art adaptation and four-frame archive clips; not a claim of exact 1:1 likeness or complete combat implementation.
